description: Call twice(6) and thrice(5) to see how each method call gets its own stack frame with its own value and result variables.

steps.description: Define twice(int value) on lines 7-11 and thrice(int value) on lines 13-17; notice that both methods name their parameter value and their local variable result.
In main, call twice(6) to assign twoTimesSix, call thrice(5) to assign threeTimesFive, and print both results.

steps.answer: Each method call creates its own stack frame with its own separate value and result variables, which disappear as soon as that method returns.
steps.question: Do twice(6) and thrice(5) share the same value and result variables in memory, or does each call get its own separate copy?

steps.description: Look at the twice stack frame on line 10 (where value = 6 and result = 12), which is replaced by a fresh thrice stack frame when thrice(5) runs on line 21.

title: Parameter Binding and Local Variable Scope
